_purpose: Which existing assessment a new one should copy its settings from, per assignment kind. MyOpenMath already has a 'copy options from' picker on the new-assessment form, so the preset is a POINTER to a template assessment, not a replayed list of fields. Nothing to keep in step when MOM adds a setting.
_how: On a push, look up the assignment's `kind`. Set `copyfrom` to that kind's template_aid, leave `copydates` UNCHECKED so dates stay per-assignment, then set the name and the dates. No template for the kind = ask Steve to set one assessment up the way he wants, then record it here.
_note: Templates are per course. If cid changes, the template_aid for that kind has to be re-pointed — an aid from another course will not appear in the copyfrom list.

due_date_rule._status: PROVISIONAL — stand-in until the real class schedule exists. Steve will replace this once the term calendar is set.
due_date_rule.provisional_meaning: the next day; if that lands on a Saturday or Sunday, the following Monday
due_date_rule.open_date: the day it is pushed, 12:00 am

_spec_note: A kind with `template_aid: null` has no template in the course yet. Its `spec` says how to BUILD that template once — set one assessment up that way by hand, then record its aid and drop the spec. Specs for ind/group/practice were harvested from the mom repo's own skills (`mom-{ind-test,group-test,practice-test}`) and have NOT been verified against a live MOM form here. `lab` has no spec anywhere; Steve has to decide what a lab is before one can be written.

hw.template_name: 1.1 Definitions of Statistics, Probability, and Key Terms
hw.summary: Shown by dates but always available, stays open for practice after the due date, 3 attempts per question with no penalty, up to 1 late pass usable after the due date, answers after the last attempt.
hw.selection: Cover the section closely — every sub-topic gets a slot before any gets a second. Where a sub-topic is a multi-step process, either write one multipart covering the whole workflow or split it into one question per step so students drill each; mix both freely. Homework is the most creative format. Ramp easy to hard, roughly 30/50/20.

lab.template_name: 1.1 Definitions of Statistics, Probability, and Key Terms
lab._decision: Steve's call: a lab is graded like practice work, so it uses the SAME template as homework rather than getting one of its own. Recorded here so it reads as a decision, not as a kind that was never set up. If labs ever need their own settings, point this at a new template — nothing else changes.
lab.selection: One lab per chapter, mirroring the book's lab section.

spec.penalty: 33% reduction after the first full-score attempt — a perfect first try is locked in, but any later attempt loses ground
spec.show_solutions: after the last attempt (never during attempts 1-2)

ind.selection: About 10 questions: ~8 high-impact FULL multipart items — each exercising every step of a process, one per chapter section, no narrow drill questions — plus exactly 2 free-response. The FRQs should touch the widest swath of the chapter AND sit at the easy end; they exist to give an accessible essay path, not to gate the grade. Budget ~5 min per multipart, ~10 min per FRQ. 10 questions x 10 pts = 100.

spec.penalty: none — groups may re-submit for a second look, but 1 version stops them rerolling for an easier draw
spec.gbcategory: Tests (or a Group Work category if the course has one)
spec.show_solutions: never, or after the due date
spec.displaymethod: all questions on one page — the group works the whole thing together

group.selection: A focused subset of the practice/test material, sized for one class period of collaborative work.

practice.selection: Assemble from questions already in the bank first; draft only to fill what is genuinely missing. Low stakes, so breadth beats polish.
